---
title: "Designing a two-condition single-cell proteomics experiment"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Designing a two-condition single-cell proteomics experiment}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(scpPower)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
seed <- 20261013L
preset <- "leduc2022_pSCoPE"
path <- system.file("presets", paste0(preset, ".yaml"), package="scpPower")
registered <- yaml::read_yaml(path)
validation <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "tmt-validation.csv", package="scpPower"))
depth <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "validation-depth.csv", package="scpPower"))
depth <- depth[depth$mask=="aggregated", ]
ratio <- depth$observed_depth_sd / depth$simulated_mean_depth_sd
power_limit <- max(validation$observed_power, na.rm=TRUE)
```

Start with the carrier-TMT Leduc preset and ask whether increasing biological
samples helps detect a twofold change at a fixed cell budget. These are planning
estimates under the preset assumptions, within the limited validation range
reported below. The example uses `r seed` as its recorded random seed.

```{r simulate}
n <- 4L
m <- 16L
fold_change <- 2
simulated <- scp_simulate(NULL, n, m, beta=log2(fold_change),
                         preset=preset, seed=seed)
dim(simulated$matrix)
head(simulated$cell_metadata)
```

The matrix has `r nrow(simulated$matrix)` proteins and
`r ncol(simulated$matrix)` cells. Biological-sample, acquisition-batch and cell
noise are simulated on the log2 scale; missing values remain missing. Joint
resampling retains each protein's abundance, variance and detection parameters.

```{r power}
replicates <- 20L
n_options <- c(4L, 8L)
planning <- scp_power(preset, n_options, m, beta=log2(fold_change),
                      replicates=replicates, seed=seed)
columns <- c("n_per_condition", "m_cells_per_sample", "power", "testability",
             "conditional_power", "realised_fdr", "instrument_hours")
knitr::kable(planning$results[, columns], digits=3)
```

These demonstration runs use `r replicates` replicates; increase that argument
for a more precise estimate and read `simulation_se` beside power. Instrument
hours count occupied batches using the preset's
`r registered$minutes_per_run` minutes per run and exclude unreported overhead.

Unconditional power divides detected changed proteins by all changed proteins.
Testability counts proteins with enough quantified cells in every biological
sample for the registered endpoint. Conditional power divides detected changed
proteins by changed proteins that are testable within a replicate; it is
undefined in replicates with none. Missingness can therefore cap unconditional
power even when conditional power is high. Per-sample means are tested with
limma-trend, and sign agreement is required for a changed protein's detection.
Read realised FDR beside rejection counts to recognise nearly empty tests:

```{r rejections}
knitr::kable(planning$results[, c("n_per_condition", "mean_rejections",
                                "zero_rejection_fraction")], digits=3)
```

Carrier compression is supplied as an assumption. Compare the registered
sensitivities at one design, without treating them as measured coefficients:

```{r sensitivity}
k_values <- c(1, 0.75, 0.5)
sensitivity <- scp_power(preset, n, m, beta=log2(fold_change), k=k_values,
                         replicates=replicates, seed=seed)
knitr::kable(sensitivity$results[, c("k", columns[-c(1,2)])], digits=3)
```

Each output records its seed, hashes, versions and wall time. Differences from
preset software versions generate a warning and the run continues.

```{r manifest}
planning$manifest$versions
planning$manifest$input_hashes
planning$manifest$wall_seconds
vignette_manifest <- list(seed=seed, versions=planning$manifest$versions,
  input_hashes=list(preset=digest::digest(file=path, algo="sha256"),
    validation=digest::digest(validation, algo="sha256"),
    depth=digest::digest(depth, algo="sha256")),
  simulation=simulated$manifest, power=planning$manifest,
  sensitivity=sensitivity$manifest, wall_seconds=proc.time()[["elapsed"]]-started)
saveRDS(vignette_manifest, "vignette-run-manifest.rds")
```

Before choosing a design, retain these limitations:

1. Between-donor variance is mapped from whole-PBMC bulk data. Its transfer to
   single cells is an assumption that requires a pilot in your own cell type.
2. Compression defaults to `r registered$k`; the sensitivity assumptions are
   `r paste(k_values[-1], collapse=" and ")`. Neither donor transfer nor
   compression is validated by the semi-synthetic exercise.
3. Real-cell carrier-TMT validation reaches observed power of about
   `r format(round(power_limit, 2), nsmall=2)`; it does not establish accuracy
   above that range.
4. Cell-depth dependence is omitted: observed depth SD is
   `r paste(format(round(ratio, 2), nsmall=2), collapse=" to ")` times the
   independent simulation's SD. This did not affect the registered validation
   verdict; correlated missingness remains a limitation.
5. Q Exactive and timsTOF public cells cannot validate designs at useful power.
6. The primary endpoint uses per-sample means and limma-trend. Other tests can
   give different power estimates.
